claim: CodeVetter can partition one selected Node request's current-process CPU into exact request-handling-thread and other-thread deltas, reconcile compatible Worker CPU inside the other-thread residual, and select a durable next probe without presenting child-process CPU as part of that residual or granting edit authority.

proofs: Process counter intervals enclose current-thread counter intervals at admission, response commitment, and request finish.
Legacy, unsupported, incomplete, malformed, negative, excessive, and inconsistent thread evidence fails closed.
Exact current-thread CPU owns main-versus-other thread routing while compatible V8 samples only name scope.
Worker CPU is divided by other-thread CPU when exact evidence exists and over-accounting requests recapture.
No current-process residual classification or next probe presents child-process CPU as a possible explanation.

diagnosis.basis: exact current-thread CPU crossed the 50% process-CPU threshold and compatible V8 samples selected runtime scope

limitations: Sequential process and thread snapshots enclose rather than exactly coincide; the result is a bounded counter partition, not instruction-level accounting.
Other-thread CPU can include Worker threads, V8 background work, libuv threadpool work, native addons, and runtime background activity; this slice does not attribute the 180.539 ms residual further.
Child processes are excluded from process.cpuUsage() and therefore require a separate end-to-end flow cost contract.
The runtime disables repository Next configuration and does not establish production-build equivalence.
The existing browser assertion failed, so the evidence authorizes no source edit, optimization, correctness, or production claim.
